headline: Muse gets voice and video chat in the US
dek: The Muse avatar talks in real time, per The Verge and TechCrunch.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Muse with an avatar
body: Meta rolled out real-time voice and video chat with the Muse avatar, its AI agent, to everyone in the United States, per The Verge and TechCrunch.
The avatar reacts with expressions and gestures that follow the tone of the talk.

points.t: Default avatar Jolly can become a person or an animal.
Tone changes by asking the agent or in settings.
The avatar only listens and cannot see users (TechCrunch).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Two new models
body: The feature runs on Muse Realtime Avatar and Muse Realtime Voice, per TechCrunch.
Before, only a limited group in the US had access, per both sources.

items.t: Coming soon to Meta's AI glasses (The Verge).
Also headed to the unreleased Muse Charm (TechCrunch).
Already works on the web and Mac (TechCrunch).

caption.hook: Meta rolled out Muse voice mode and video chat with its AI avatar to everyone in the US.
body: Per The Verge and TechCrunch, the avatar reacts with expressions and gestures while it talks. The default is called Jolly and can become another look, from a person to an animal. Voice tone changes by asking the agent or in settings. The avatar does not use the camera: it only listens to what is said.

TechCrunch says the feature runs on two new models, Muse Realtime Avatar and Muse Realtime Voice, and also works on the web and Mac. Before, only a limited group in the US had access. Meta says the feature is coming soon to its AI glasses and to the Muse Charm, a wearable that has not launched yet.
caption.cta: Would you video chat with an AI avatar?
